class.name: PlayerController
class.brief_description: A human's controller: it possesses a pawn and owns that player's input.
class.description: It exists on the server for every player and on each client for that client's own player, and nowhere else - which is what makes it the right place to send a player's input from, and the wrong place to keep anything everyone has to see. On possession it calls [code]_setup_input_component[/code] on the [Pawn], which is where input actions get bound, and makes the pawn camera current where the player is actually sitting. It belongs to a level and dies with it. The human behind it is the [LocalPlayer], which the [GameInstance] owns and which survives [method World.load_level] - that is where the device assignment and the split screen viewport live. In a networked game the owning client sends what its player is holding and the server applies it to this controller's [PlayerInput], so the input component and the pawn run the same code in every net mode. Input from any peer other than [method Controller.get_owner_peer_id] is dropped.

method.name: get_input_component
method.description: The component built for the possessed pawn, through which its bindings run. Null while nothing is possessed.

method.name: get_local_player
method.description: The human this controller belongs to. Null on the server for a player sitting at another machine, and on a dedicated server for everyone. It is owned by the [GameInstance], so it outlives this controller across a level change.

method.name: get_player_input
method.description: The action state this controller reads: a local player's own state, or - on the server, for a player at another machine - the state that player's client last sent.

method.name: get_player_viewport
method.description: [member LocalPlayer.viewport_override] if the player has one, otherwise this node viewport.

method.name: is_local_player_controller
method.description: Always true today. The hook exists so code written now stays correct once a client owns only a subset of the world controllers.

method.name: register_input_component
method.description: Adds the component to this controller input stack and points it at this controller, which is how it finds the right [PlayerInput].

method.name: server_receive_input
method.description: Remote call: the owning client's action state, written into this controller's [PlayerInput] on the server. From the input component down the server then runs exactly the code a local player runs. Input sent for a controller the sender does not own is dropped.

method.name: set_local_player
method.description: Binds this controller to a human at this machine. The framework does this on login.

method.name: set_owner_peer_id
method.description: Sets which connection this controller answers to. The framework assigns it on login; remote calls from any other peer are dropped.

method.name: set_pawn_camera_node_as_current
method.description: Makes the possessed pawn's camera current in this player's viewport. Called on possession unless [member Pawn.auto_manage_camera] is false. [b]Warns when the pawn has no camera[/b], which is the expected shape for a game filmed by a camera the level owns - turn [member Pawn.auto_manage_camera] off there.

method.name: unregister_input_component
method.description: Takes a component out of this controller's input stack. Safe to call from inside a binding.

members.member: Which input actions are sent to the server. [b]Empty means every action in the input map that is not a built-in [code]ui_[/code] one[/b] - narrow it to what gameplay actually needs and the per-frame traffic shrinks with it.

signal.name: local_player_changed
signal.description: This controller was bound to a different human, or to none.
